claims.claim_text: Indexed Major Charles Vanda is high-confidence matched to radio executive Charles Vanda, who served in Army Intelligence during World War II.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: UNLV's finding aid links the rare exact name, broadcast career and wartime Army Intelligence service; the index supplies a compatible Major rank.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence from rare exact name, compatible rank and authoritative wartime-service context.
claims.temporal_assessment: The same institutional chronology places his CBS career before and alongside wartime service.
claims.match_notes: The sources do not establish a precise OSS accession date or the reason the indexed personnel file was created.

claims.claim_text: CBS Radio is Charles Vanda's last documented civilian employer before his wartime Army Intelligence service.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: UNLV dates his CBS appointment to 1935 and later wartime Army Intelligence work; the Los Angeles Times independently confirms the CBS role and career chronology.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High-confidence rare-name, broadcast-career and wartime-service match.
claims.temporal_assessment: Probable last civilian employer before military service; the exact leave and formal employment dates remain unresolved.
claims.match_notes: Not presented as an explicit direct transfer into OSS; the site preserves the distinction between last civilian employer and immediate pre-OSS affiliation.

claims.claim_text: Indexed Amry Vandenbosch is high-confidence matched to the University of Kentucky political scientist who served in the State Department and OSS.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The rare exact name, university career and explicit institutional OSS statement align with a 1943 State Department memorandum he authored.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence from rare exact name, authoritative institutional career evidence and official wartime government documentation.
claims.temporal_assessment: The sources document university employment before State and OSS service but do not fully order the wartime assignments.
claims.match_notes: The State Department and OSS assignments are not collapsed into one relationship.

claims.claim_text: The University of Kentucky was Amry Vandenbosch's last documented civilian employer before his State Department and OSS service.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: UK dates his department-head tenure from 1933; a 1943 State Department memorandum and UK history document his later government and OSS service.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High-confidence rare-name and continuous institutional-career match.
claims.temporal_assessment: Probable last civilian employer; the exact leave date and State-to-OSS sequence remain unresolved.
claims.match_notes: Not labeled an immediate OSS predecessor because State Department service may have intervened.

claims.claim_text: Indexed Hoyt S Vandenberg is confirmed as Army Air Forces officer Hoyt S. Vandenberg.

claims.temporal_assessment: The register documents his Army career through 1942 but does not establish OSS service or explain the indexed file.
claims.match_notes: The officer number remains private; Box 798 review is required before asserting any OSS assignment or pre-OSS transition.
